security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, standard Dockerfile commands, Kubernetes configuration examples, and defensive security tooling. One issue is confirmed: the Dockerfile example includes a build-time outbound request to a placeholder external scanning service, which is unsafe for users to copy without verification.

remediation.issue: Dockerfile example calls an external security scanning URL during image build.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the outbound urllib.request build step or replace it with a documented local scanner command that users run explicitly.

remediation.issue: Some hardening snippets use broad system-level commands inside example Dockerfiles.
remediation.suggestion: Add short caution text that examples should be tested against each base image before production use.

content.user_title: Build Secure Docker and Kubernetes Deployments
content.value_statement: Container deployments need repeatable security controls across images, clusters, networking, and operations. This skill provides Docker and Kubernetes patterns that help Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft hardened production configurations.
actual_capabilities: Draft multi-stage Dockerfile patterns with non-root users and minimal runtime images.
Create Kubernetes namespace, RBAC, deployment, service account, and network policy examples.
Suggest Istio service mesh configuration for mutual TLS, retries, timeouts, and traffic routing.
Outline ArgoCD GitOps application settings for automated sync and deployment recovery.
Provide Prometheus alerting examples and a production deployment security checklist.
limitations: Examples require review before use in a real cluster or registry.
Cloud-specific identity, ingress, and secret settings must be adapted by the user.
The skill does not run scanners, deploy workloads, or validate manifests by itself.
Some commands are illustrative and may not work with every base image.

use_cases.title: Harden a new container image
use_cases.description: Generate a multi-stage Dockerfile with smaller runtime layers, non-root execution, health checks, and cleanup steps.
use_cases.target_user: Backend engineers preparing services for production containers

use_cases.title: Create secure Kubernetes manifests
use_cases.description: Draft RBAC, deployment, network policy, service account, and security context examples for an application namespace.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineers building application deployment templates

use_cases.title: Plan production operations controls
use_cases.description: Use service mesh, GitOps, monitoring, and checklist examples to cover deployment safety and observability.
use_cases.target_user: DevOps teams standardizing cluster release practices

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic secure Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-k8s skill to create a secure multi-stage Dockerfile for a Python web API. Include a non-root user, dependency caching, health checks, and runtime cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Kubernetes hardening manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-k8s skill to draft Kubernetes manifests for my service. Include namespace labels, RBAC, a restricted service account, deployment securityContext, probes, and a default-deny network policy.

prompt_templates.title: Add GitOps and observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-k8s skill to design an ArgoCD deployment flow with Prometheus alerts for a production Kubernetes service. Explain which values I must replace for my environment.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production deployment plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the docker-k8s skill to review my Dockerfile and Kubernetes deployment plan for production readiness. Focus on image security, RBAC, network policy, secrets, service mesh, and monitoring gaps.

output_examples.input: Create a secure Dockerfile for a Python API.
output: A multi-stage build plan with separate builder and runtime stages.
A non-root runtime user and restricted file permissions.
Health check and dependency cleanup guidance.

output_examples.input: Harden my Kubernetes deployment for production.
output: A namespace and RBAC outline using least privilege.
Network policy and service account settings to reduce default access.

output_examples.input: Prepare GitOps and monitoring for a service.
output: An ArgoCD application structure with sync policy notes.
Prometheus alert ideas for errors, unauthorized access, and restarts.
A checklist of values to customize before applying manifests.

best_practices: Replace every placeholder registry, domain, repository, and secret reference before using generated manifests.
Validate Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests with your approved scanners before deployment.
Start with least privilege RBAC and default-deny network policies, then add only required access.
anti_patterns: Do not copy production examples directly without adapting namespaces, identities, and resource limits.
Do not run external build-time security services unless your organization has approved them.
Do not grant broad cluster permissions when namespace-scoped permissions are enough.

faq.question: Can this skill deploy to my cluster automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and draft configurations. You must review and apply them with your own deployment tools.

faq.question: Does it support Docker and Kubernetes together?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers container image construction and Kubernetes deployment patterns for production services.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Are the manifests ready for production?
faq.answer: They are starting points. You must adapt values, test policies, and validate them against your platform requirements.

faq.question: Does it include service mesh guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Istio-style examples for mutual TLS, routing, retries, and traffic controls.

faq.question: How should I handle secrets with this skill?
faq.answer: Use the examples as references for secret references only. Do not place real secret values in prompts or generated files.
